newsitem.title: SPAIN: Madrid stocks close 2 pct lower, Telefonica drags.
newsitem.headline: Madrid stocks close 2 pct lower, Telefonica drags.

text.p: Madrid stocks ended sharply lower on Monday, hit by a slide on foreign share and bond markets and amid particular weakness in Telefonica, dealers said.
The general index fell 8.27 points, 1.70 percent, to 476.93 and the Ibex-35 shed 109.42 points, 1.97 percent, to 5,458.63.
Telefonica dropped 125 pesetas to 3,340 amid selling from final clients abroad, worried that the firm would be forced to charge its future competitor Retevision less than anticipated.

"It seems the government, having forced (second operator) Retevision to be privatised long before it is really ready, is now going to compensate the firm by approving a cheap connection charge, which would mean substantially less income for Telefonica, and stronger competition," said a trader.
Repsol rose 60 pesetas to 6,030 on strong demand ahead of the April sale of the state's last 10 percent in the firm.

In general the market has been hit by fears of rise in U.S. key money rates, which has made for erratic trading eyeing Wall Street. The outlook will continue volatile until this is resolved, dealers said.
